name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: REST APIs that let Amazon selling partners automate orders, shipments, pricing, and inventory.
auth_notes: Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth 2.0. Public apps get seller authorization through the OAuth workflow. Private apps self-authorize in the Solution Provider Portal and get an LWA refresh token, which must be renewed annually.
access_notes: Developers register in the Solution Provider Portal and must request and qualify for roles. Restricted roles that expose PII need enhanced security. Public apps need Amazon approval to publish to the Selling Partner Appstore. Cost is not stated on the fetched pages.

buildability.rationale: Documented REST APIs with a sandbox and LWA OAuth. Role qualification (restricted roles for PII) and public app approval gate production credentials.

identity.quote: The SP-API offers a collection of REST-based APIs that you can use to automate selling operations

auth.quote: Public applications must use OAuth 2.0 to obtain authorization from selling partners to call the SP-API on the selling partner's behalf.

access.quote: When you create a developer account, you must request and qualify for the specific roles that align with your intended use of the SP-API.

sandbox.quote: A test environment for trying SP-API operations.

api_surface.quote: Restrictions on the number of API requests that you can make in a specific timeframe.

mcp.quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides AI agents with access to Amazon Seller Central data through the Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API).

needs_human_reason: Role qualification timing and whether the target app is public or private are unresolved. Endpoint counts, pagination and pricing are not on the fetched pages. Only a community MCP server was found.
